finding: When Jev had to build code, the right piece was not among its options: built-in functions like map were offered only as bare names, never as calls such as map(?, ?). Jev correctly gave up 14 times.
change: Offer every in-scope function whose result fits the hole as a call with the right number of blanks, built-ins included.

finding: Half-finished builds were left in the program, so the full-Jev run ended with a broken definition and no value.
change: Make Jev edits all-or-nothing: if any blank is still open at the end, restore the original and tell the planner which blanks are open.

finding: Jev was offered options that can never be right, such as re-defining an existing function's name.
change: Only offer new-name forms for names the planner declares as new.

finding: Neither setup said DONE. Control met the goal early but kept editing until the 24-turn cap; the full-Jev run repeated the same failing request 14 times.
change: Stop a run when the goal is met; nudge the planner after two identical failures.

finding: Jev picked the view well on the small program: its very first selection, from the user's message alone, opened exactly the two definitions that needed fixing.
change: None needed; kept as the reference behaviour.

finding: On the 61-definition fleet program, Jev as navigator cost 48% more and took 55% longer than control. The planner's requests named 2 or 3 definitions, but Jev opened 6 to 53 of them (6% precision): "relevant" was too loose a question.
change: Tried (untested guess): stricter question + a 0.8 cutoff on Jev's yes + open paths the request names. The cutoff was later removed (see Eval 003).

finding: Every navigation request replaced the whole view, so the planner asked one definition at a time and re-asked: 18 requests and 6 extra turns.
change: Navigation requests add to the view by default, and the tool asks for everything at once.

finding: The test requests named the exact definitions to fix, so control found them with three clicks and navigation was never hard. Jev could only add cost.
change: Added symptoms-only versions of the fleet, depot and warranty tests that describe what users see and never name the code.

finding: Jev was not free at this size: each navigation request sent all 61 definitions (about 11k tokens), 24% of the run's cost. Its own time was only about 6 s in total; the slowdown was extra, slower planner turns.
change: Planned: send one-line headers for far-away definitions and full code only for likely candidates.

finding: A test clean-up command deleted a paid run's results folder; Eval 001's numbers were recovered from captured output.
change: Tests write to temporary folders; nothing deletes results.

finding: On the big program with named bugs, the Jev navigator fixed all three bugs correctly but was scored a fail: the planner replaced the program's final line with its own checks, so the value no longer matched.
change: Grade by checking each fix (tests on the fixed functions) instead of the exact final value, and tell the planner not to change the final line.

finding: Jev still opened far too much (about 5-6% of what it opened was needed, same as Eval 002). Eval 003 changed several things at once, so we can't tell which helped or hurt.
change: Removed the extra 0.8 cutoff: we now take Jev's own yes/no. Next: measure Jev's picks directly (no planner) and change one thing at a time, starting with the question wording.

finding: Symptom-only task: both setups fixed everything. Jev used fewer view calls (15 vs 19) but cost 41% more and took 20% longer; Jev itself was 19% of the run's cost.
change: No win yet for the navigator on cost or speed.

finding: All three runs used all 40 turns and never said DONE, even after the goal was met.
change: Stop the run when the goal is met (pending).

finding: Jev builds code fixed the named-bug fleet program 2/2, 22% cheaper than the original; 0/4 on the other tests.
change: Hypothesis: works when the fix is clear and local. Next: more runs, and offer calls like map(?, ?).

finding: Jev navigates was correct 8/8; same cost on 2 of 3 tests, +32% on the symptoms-only test, and slower on all.
change: Cheaper Jev requests (send summaries, not full code) are the main lever.
